subject: dinterval returns non-integer values for latent state that follows a discrete distribution

messages.author: 46f76d1903dc6874
messages.subject: dinterval returns non-integer values for latent state that follows a discrete distribution
parts:
I'm getting some strange behavior with dinterval in a nimble model.

Here's the relevant code in the nimble model:

# Likelihood
for (n in 1:N) {
   prob[n, 1:time_steps] <- ilogit(X[n, , ] %*% Beta[])
   censored[n] ~ dinterval(z[n], y[n, 1:2])
   z[n] ~ dtvgeom_nimble(prob[n, 1:time_steps])
            
   y_rep[n] ~ dtvgeom_nimble(prob[n, 1:time_steps])
}

dtvgeom_nimble is registered as a discrete distribution:

registerDistributions(list(
  dtvgeom_nimble = list(
    BUGSdist = "dtvgeom_nimble(prob)",
    pqAvail = TRUE,
    discrete = TRUE,
    range = c(1, Inf),
    types = c("prob = double(1)")
  )), verbose = F, userEnv = .GlobalEnv)


When I monitor z in the output, I'm seeing non-integer values. Monitoring y_rep shows (correctly) integer values only, so I'm assuming it must have something to do with invoking dinterval. Any idea what might be going on?

Thanks for any insight!

- Vincent

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: dinterval returns non-integer values for latent state that follows a discrete distribution
parts:
Honestly, I can't imagine any way in which the fact that z[n] is provided as an argument to dinterval() would affect the sampling of z.  I'm perplexed because you do specify the (custom) dtvgeom_nimble distribution using discrete=TRUE, so it shouldn't get sampled in any way to generate non-integers.

I'd be happy to look at this, but would need a reproducible example to see what's actually happening.  Also, the definition for the log-dentisy of dtvgeom_nimble will be (necessary, and) insightful.

Cheers,
Daniel

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: dinterval returns non-integer values for latent state that follows a discrete distribution
parts:
Vincent, this was an interesting investigation.

I wish I had a better understanding of the internals of the doParallel package, and similarly foreach.  But I can confirm that with your current code, when the multiple (>1) workers are instantiated and deployed using makeCluster() and registerDoParallel(), those instances are not finding the distribution registration that you did earlier.  As a result, in each instance, a (normally default) RW sampler is being assigned to each z[], thus giving rise to non-integer samples.

I tried another approach, and put the registerDistributions() call inside the foreach() call, inside your definition of the tempo_mcmc() function.  The (very simply) modified code is below.  I checked that now slice samplers were assigned to the z[]'s, which is nimble's default sampler for discrete-valued latent states.  Indeed, now it works as intended, and the posterior samples for the z[]'s are all integer-valued.  So I think this fixes your problem.

There are certainly some interesting questions here about scoping and interplay between packages.  But barring those, I hope the code below will get you moving again.

Cheers, and thanks for your use and interest in nimble,
Daniel


out <- foreach(i = 1:n_chains,
               .combine = list,
               .packages = c("nimble", "tempo"),
               .multicombine = TRUE) %dopar% {
                   pheno_model <- suppressMessages(
                       nimbleModel(code = eval(parse(text = tempo:::nimble_model(beta_random_indices,
                                                         correlated))),
                                   name = "pheno",
                                   constants = inputs$pheno_consts,
                                   data = inputs$pheno_data,
                                   inits = inputs$pheno_inits # TODO: [[i]] # different inits for each chain
                                   )
                   )
                   suppressWarnings(registerDistributions(list(

dtvgeom_nimble = list(
                           BUGSdist = "dtvgeom_nimble(prob)",
                           pqAvail = TRUE,
                           discrete = TRUE,
                           range = c(1, Inf),
                           types = c("prob = double(1)")

)), verbose = F, userEnv = .GlobalEnv))
                   mcmc_cfg <- configureMCMC(pheno_model,
                                             monitors = monitors)
                   samp <- mcmc_cfg$getSamplers()
                   pheno_mcmc <- buildMCMC(mcmc_cfg)
                   compiled_mcmc <- suppressMessages(compileNimble(pheno_model,
                                                                   pheno_mcmc))
                   out_temp <- runMCMC(compiled_mcmc$pheno_mcmc,
                                       niter = n_iter + n_burnin,
                                       nburnin = n_burnin)
                   return(list(out_temp, samp))
               }
stopCluster(cl)
